title: Built-In Electric Field Modulation of Spontaneous Magnetism and Thermospin Transport in Boron-Nitrogen Doped Zigzag Graphene Nanoribbons
authors: Ma Luo, Yiyi Xie, Xinxiu Wu
abstract: Zigzag-edged graphene nanoribbons (ZGNRs) host large magnetic moments at two zigzag edges due to spontaneous magnetism, whose ground state is antiferromagnetically coupled spin-order edge state (AF state). In this paper, the spontaneous magnetism and thermoelectricity of ZGNRs with periodic substituted doping of boron and nitrogen atoms along the axial direction are investigated by first principle calculation. The doping induces an internal electric field, which modulates the magnetic moments at the two zigzag edges and the band structure with spin splitting. For varying doping configuration, the ground state could be AF state, ferromagnetically coupled spin-order edge state (FM state), or degenerated pair of AF and FM states. External transversal static electric field can further modulate the magnetic moments and the band structure. By designing the doping configuration and the external field, pure thermal spin current with the absence of thermal charge current can be generated at room temperature, which can be switched on and off by flipping the magnetic configuration between AF and FM states. Thus, the doped ZGNRs can be applied as prototype devices for spin-caloritronic.
summary: This theoretical study uses DFT to model B-N doped ZGNRs, showing that doping induces an internal electric field that controls the magnetic ground state between AF and FM. By combining doping design with an external electric field, the authors propose a robust, switchable prototype device capable of generating pure thermal spin current for spintronic applications.
main_problem: The study investigates how built-in electric fields, induced by B-N doping, modulate the spontaneous magnetism and resulting thermospin transport in Zigzag Graphene Nanoribbons (ZGNRs). The goal is to create a switchable device for pure thermal spin current generation.
main_result: By engineering the doping configuration and applying an external electric field, the system can switch between Antiferromagnetic (AF) and Ferromagnetic (FM) states, enabling the generation and switching of a pure thermal spin current at room temperature.
method: The research relies on first-principle Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations, using supercell models to simulate the electronic and magnetic properties.
model_or_system: The physical system is a Zigzag Graphene Nanoribbon (ZGNR) periodically doped with Boron and Nitrogen atoms. The model explores the magnetic ground state (AF vs. FM) and the resulting spin-split band structure under applied electric fields.
key_observables: Total energy difference ($\Delta E$) between AF and FM states, band gaps, spin polarization distribution, and pure thermal spin current.
important_parameters: Doping configuration ($k_N, k_B$), external transversal static electric field strength, and temperature (room temperature operation).
main_assumptions: The doping system maintains overall electrical neutrality, and the calculations use DFT with GGA-PBE functional approximations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the doped ZGNR structure, the dependence of energy differences ($\Delta E$) on doping geometry, and the resulting band structures for different magnetic states.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the magnetic ground state based on doping patterns, then examines how external electric fields further modulate the band structure and achieve the desired pure spin current switching functionality.
why_interesting: While primarily condensed matter physics, the concept of using electric fields to switch magnetic states (magnetoelectric coupling) and generate pure spin currents is highly relevant to open quantum systems and spintronics research.
